patch_description: The current pair-move hill-climb only moves the single closest and single farthest pair. Two upgrades inspired by the binding-constraint structure of the optimal Tammes-like configurations: (1) consider several near-minimal and near-maximal pairs (often the optimum has multiple simultaneously-binding constraints — e.g. several edges tied at dmin in the D6/ring family), moving each along its connecting direction; (2) after the hill-climb, re-anneal the result at low temperature with L-BFGS-B (the hill-climb point is generally not a local optimum of the smooth objective, and re-annealing lets all 14 coordinates relax), then hill-climb again — alternate for a few rounds. This closes the gap the coordinate moves cannot reach while keeping runtime bounded. I also slightly reduce Phase 2/3 work to compensate for the added time.
